item.title: From Pongal To Tilgul: A Journey Through India’s Harvest Festival Foods
item.description: From Pongal To Tilgul: How India Celebrates The Harvest On Makar Sankranti From sweet pongal and tilgul to pitha and khichdi, Makar Sankranti is a reminder that India’s harvest festivals are written in food: seasonal, local, and deeply rooted.

item.description: UP Warriorz Partner With Ekaya Banaras For A Handloom-Inspired Jersey Titled 'A Blooming Rebellion', the jersey draws from floral motifs commonly found in Banarasi textiles.

item.title: From Kashmiri Pinjra-kari To Rajasthan's Jharokas: Windows That Tell India’s Stories
item.description: A Look At 6 Of India’s Traditional Windows, Region By Region From jharokhas and pinjra kari to Chettinad stained glass and louvred windows, explore India’s disappearing vernacular window styles and their stories.

item.title: The Gathering Is Redefining What A Contemporary Indian Cultural Festival Can Be
item.description: Why The Gathering Is India’s Most Thoughtful Food, Art & Culture Festival Mumbai’s Mukesh Mills transforms into a high-concept cultural arena for the festival’s second edition — where food, art, and ideas unfold through unique experiences.

item.title: 'Goopi Gawaiya Bagha Bajaiya' Is Karadi Tales’ Animated Love Letter To Indian Stories
item.description: From Colonial Folktale to Animated Classic: The Enduring World of Goopy and Bagha Tracing the journey of Goopy and Bagha from a colonial-era folktale to Karadi Tales’ animated adaptation, and the impact on Indian storytelling, childhood, and cultural identity.

item.description: This Week In Culture: Inside India’s Changing Art, Food & Music Landscapes From Himalayan land art and Banarasi handloom jerseys to Karshni Nair’s new music and Kolkata’s evolving food scene — this week’s culture round-up charts India in flux.

item.title: In Conversation With Jessie Sohpaul: Diaspora, Caste, & Making Art That Refuses Comfort
item.description: How Jessie Sohpaul Is Reimagining Punjabi Diasporic Identity Through Art Punjabi-Canadian artist Jessie Sohpaul speaks on diaspora, caste, public art, and responsibility — why discomfort is essential to honest cultural work.

item.description: How Contemporary Artists Are Reworking Carnatic Music Across Rock, Indie & Electronic Sounds Today, artists trained in Carnatic music are using this framework to speak about identity, politics and belonging.

item.description: Girls Skate Hyderabad Is Changing Who Skateboarding Is For From workshops to community-building, 'Girls Skate Hyderabad' is carving out space for women and queer skaters in a male-dominated scene.

item.description: ‘Little Fishies’ Reflects On How Societal Norms Shape Grief In Indian Families Underneath the rituals, 'Little Fishies' is a juxtaposition of the age-old society vs the individual debate and how it manifests within a family system.
